shortDescription: Olódùmarè is the supreme being, creator, and source of all existence in Yoruba religion, embodying ultimate power and wisdom.

extendedContent.title: Origins & Mythology
extendedContent.content: In Yoruba cosmology, Olódùmarè is the primordial source from which all things originate. The creation narratives vary, but they often involve Olódùmarè delegating tasks to other deities. One common myth tells of Obatala being tasked with creating land from the primordial waters. After Obatala's initial attempt, Olódùmarè provided the necessary power to solidify the land, creating the earth. Similarly, when Obatala sculpted the first humans, it was Olódùmarè who breathed life into them. Olódùmarè's role is thus one of ultimate origin and empowerment, setting the stage for the actions of the other deities and the unfolding of the universe. Olódùmarè embodies the concept of absolute beginning, the uncaused cause of all that exists.

extendedContent.title: Role & Significance
extendedContent.content: Olódùmarè's role in Yoruba religion is that of the supreme authority and ultimate source of power. While the Orishas are more actively involved in human affairs, Olódùmarè represents the overarching cosmic order and the source of Àṣẹ, the vital force that animates all things. Olódùmarè is not typically the direct recipient of worship, as devotees usually interact with the Orishas. However, the recognition of Olódùmarè's supremacy is fundamental to Yoruba belief. Olódùmarè's significance lies in the establishment of destiny and the maintenance of cosmic balance. The moral and ethical principles of Yoruba religion are rooted in the understanding of Olódùmarè's divine order and the importance of aligning oneself with Àṣẹ.

extendedContent.title: Symbolism & Interpretation
extendedContent.content: Olódùmarè is often symbolized by the sky or the heavens, representing the vastness and incomprehensibility of the divine. The concept of light is also associated with Olódùmarè, symbolizing knowledge, wisdom, and the source of all creation. The number three is sometimes considered sacred to Olódùmarè, representing the trinity of existence: the physical, the spiritual, and the divine. Interpretations of Olódùmarè vary, but the common thread is the recognition of a supreme, all-powerful being who is the source of all that exists. Olódùmarè embodies the ultimate mystery of creation and the divine order that governs the universe. The distance and abstract nature of Olódùmarè symbolize the limitations of human understanding when it comes to comprehending the absolute.

extendedContent.title: Legacy & Influence
extendedContent.content: The concept of Olódùmarè continues to be a central tenet of Yoruba religion, which has spread throughout the African diaspora, particularly in Brazil (Candomblé and Umbanda), Cuba (Santería), and the United States. The belief in a supreme creator God provides a foundation for ethical and moral principles, emphasizing the importance of living in harmony with Àṣẹ and respecting the divine order. Olódùmarè's influence extends beyond religious practices, shaping cultural values and artistic expressions. The stories and myths associated with Olódùmarè continue to inspire and provide guidance to those who follow the Yoruba tradition. The emphasis on a single, supreme being has also facilitated dialogue and understanding with other monotheistic religions.

description: Olódùmarè is the supreme God in the Yoruba religion and is considered the source of all existence. Unlike the Orishas, who are more directly involved in the daily lives of humans, Olódùmarè is more distant, representing the ultimate authority and the source of all power. Olódùmarè created the universe and all that exists within it. The creation myths often involve other deities like Obatala, who was tasked with molding the first humans from clay. However, it was Olódùmarè who breathed life into them, granting them consciousness and destiny. Olódùmarè is not typically approached directly in worship; rather, prayers and offerings are usually directed to the Orishas, who act as intermediaries. Olódùmarè's influence is pervasive, as all things ultimately originate from and are sustained by this supreme being. The concept of Àṣẹ, the divine power or life force, emanates from Olódùmarè and is the source of all action and change in the universe.
